correction.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page places the sultanate in 'the East Aceh Regency'; no frontier or area is given, so the regency is drawn as the Samudera Pasai dossier draws it (a 45 km disc on Langsa inside Aceh). The 986-988 division into Perlak Pesisir (Shia) and Perlak Pedalaman (Sunni) is a ledger event, not a shape.

region.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

ledger.note: 840: the first sultan founds Peureulak. Sultan Alaiddin Syed Maulana Abdul Aziz Shah founded the sultanate 'on 1 Muharram 225 H (840 AD)'; infobox 'Foundation 840' (the founding is traditional: the Arab scholar's mission is dated 1112 and a geographer's record 1178).

region.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

ledger.note: 986: Peureulak divides in two. After a Shia-Sunni civil war (913-915) and a four-year conflict after 956, the realm divides: Perlak Pesisir (Shia) under Sultan Alaiddin Syed Maulana Shah '(986-988)' and Perlak Pedalaman (Sunni) under Sultan Makhdum Alaiddin Malik Ibrahim Shah Johan Berdaulat '(986-1023)'. The page does not say where the line ran; the whole sultanate is given as the region.

region.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

ledger.note: 988: Perlak Pesisir ends. The Shia sultan of the coast died 'when the Kingdom of Sriwijaya invaded Perlak'; the Sunni Perlak Pedalaman, which reigned to 1023, is taken as the continuing state (the page does not say who held the coast afterwards).

region.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

ledger.note: 988: Srivijaya invades Perlak. The Shia sultan 'died when the Kingdom of Sriwijaya invaded Perlak'; Sultan Makhdum Alaiddin Malik Ibrahim Shah Johan Berdaulat 'continued the struggle against Sriwijaya until 1006'. The 988 year is the end of Perlak Pesisir's reign on the page; the Srivijaya side has no matching event (the srivijaya dossier does not mention Perlak).

region.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

ledger.note: 1006: the Perlak struggle against Srivijaya ends. 'continued the struggle against Sriwijaya until 1006'.

region.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

ledger.note: 1292: Peureulak is united with Pasai. The 18th sultan reigned '1267-1292'; 'After he died, Perlak was united with the Samudera Pasai Kingdom'; infobox 'Disestablished 1292'. The samudera-pasai-sultanate dossier carries the matching gain.

region.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

ledger.note: 1292: the Peureulak Sultanate ends in Pasai. Marco Polo had stopped 'in the state of Ferlec' in 1291; the Pasai page says only 'Two small Muslim trading kingdoms existed by that time at Pasai and Peureulak or Perlak'.

wars.name: Srivijaya's invasion of Perlak

zones.text: Peureulak, now the East Aceh Regency

wars.outcome: The Shia sultan of Perlak Pesisir died in the invasion; Sultan Makhdum 'continued the struggle against Sriwijaya until 1006'.
wars.note: The page gives no battle or territorial result; the zone is the whole sultanate.

certainty.note: The East Aceh Regency is a modern stand-in for a trading sultanate; no frontier is known.

sources.title: Peureulak Sultanate
sources.note: Infobox (840 to 1292), the Shia-Sunni division 986, Srivijaya's invasion and the struggle to 1006, the union with Pasai in 1292.

sources.title: Samudera Pasai Sultanate
sources.note: Pasai's side: Pasai and Peureulak as 'two small Muslim trading kingdoms' at the end of the 13th century; the infobox lists Peureulak as predecessor; no merger sentence on the page.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Peureulak. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The founding in 840 and the 18-sultan list are the Hikayat-based tradition the page reports; the first firm dates are the 1178 geographer's record and Marco Polo's 1291 stop at 'Ferlec'. The region is the Samudera Pasai dossier's. The Shia-Sunni division (986-988) and the Srivijaya invasion (988-1006) are the page's, with no geography and no Srivijaya-side counterpart (a gap-filler could ask the srivijaya dossier to carry it). No ruler strip: the page lists 18 sultans with reign years from 840 to 1292 but the list is traditional. Gazetteer: Peureulak/Perlak town is not in places.jsonl (Langsa is).
